label: Number of samples
tooltip: How many libraries you want to pool and sequence together on one flowcell.
detail: The tool checks whether this many samples fit on each flowcell at your requested depth, and also reports the maximum number that would fit. Index compatibility and pooling balance are not considered.

label: Read length
tooltip: Bases sequenced per read. For paired-end, enter the length of ONE mate - 2x150 means you enter 150.
detail: Determines which kit you need: total cycles are roughly read_length x 2 for PE, plus index cycles. Longer reads cost more cycles and, on some kits, fewer total reads. Some applications have a minimum (16S and amplicons need 2x300 to overlap the V3-V4 region).

label: PE / SE
tooltip: Paired-end sequences both ends of each fragment; single-end sequences one end only.
detail: PE doubles the bases per cluster, so it halves the reads needed to reach a given coverage - but it needs twice the cycles, so it costs more per read. Use PE for assembly, variants, and anything needing overlap or insert-size information; SE is usually enough for counting applications like ChIP-seq.

label: Number of reads
tooltip: Sequencing depth per sample, in millions of reads. For paired-end, one read PAIR counts as one read.
detail: This is the number of usable reads you need after QC and alignment. The tool divides by the usable read fraction to get the raw reads it must reserve on the flowcell. Under-sequencing is the most common reason a run has to be repeated - if unsure, use the application default.

label: Coverage
tooltip: Average number of times each base in the genome is sequenced. 30x means every base is read ~30 times on average.
detail: Coverage is converted to reads as: coverage x genome size / (read length x 2 for PE). Because it depends on genome size, you must set the genome size for this to be meaningful. Rough guides: 30x for germline variants, 100x+ for de novo assembly, several hundred x for low-frequency or somatic variants.

label: Genome size
tooltip: Size of the target sequence space, in megabases. This drives the coverage calculation, so a wrong value scales your whole run.
detail: Human is ~3200 Mb, E. coli ~5 Mb, yeast ~12 Mb. For a targeted panel or exome, enter the size of the TARGET region, not the whole genome - a 2 Mb panel at 500x needs far less sequencing than a 3200 Mb genome at 500x. For metagenomics this is the estimated total community size and is inherently a guess.

label: PhiX control library
tooltip: Share of the flowcell taken by the PhiX control library. These clusters are not available to your samples.
detail: PhiX has a balanced base composition (45% GC / 55% AT). Low-diversity libraries such as 16S and amplicons lack that balance, which degrades template registration and base calling, so for them the default is 40% - Illumina's recommendation for the NextSeq 1000/2000, where at least 32% of reads should align to PhiX. ATGC adds the control library as requested. That share is not available to your samples. RRBS needs a spike for the same reason. Other applications use ~2% purely for run quality monitoring. Ref: https://knowledge.illumina.com/instrumentation/general/instrumentation-general-reference_material-list/000001527

label: Usable read fraction
tooltip: Fraction of raw reads expected to survive QC, trimming, and alignment.
detail: Raw flowcell output is never all usable - reads are lost to failed filters, adapter content, duplicates, and unaligned or off-target sequence. The tool inflates your depth request by this factor so you actually receive the depth you asked for. 0.85 is a general placeholder; the real value is application- and sample-quality-dependent.
